findings.title: except Exception silently swallows gateway failures
findings.body: According to custom instructions in 'Error Handling Standards' (no except Exception that swallows an error without logging or re-raising): `execute` wraps the gateway call in `except Exception:` (line 31) and returns `None` (line 32) with no logging, context or re-raise. This differs from `ChargeRepository.save` in the same PR, which lets failures propagate. A gateway outage becomes a silent `None` with no trace in logs, indistinguishable from 'no charge happened'. Log the failure with the account id and re-raise, or return a typed result.

findings.title: get_latest does not order results, so it is not the latest
findings.body: `get_latest` (lines 29-33) selects rows for the account and calls `result.scalars().first()` (line 33) with no `order_by` on the query (line 31). Without an explicit order, SQL does not guarantee row order, so `first()` returns an arbitrary matching row, not the most recent one. This contradicts both the method name and its own docstring, 'Return the latest charge recorded for the account'. Any caller that relies on `get_latest` for the current charge state (a status check, a duplicate-charge guard) can act on a stale or random row. Add `.order_by(ChargeRow.created_at.desc())` (or the equivalent recency column) and `.limit(1)` before calling `first()`.

findings.title: ChargeRepository has no test coverage in this diff
findings.body: According to custom instructions in 'Test Coverage for Complex Functions' (new or changed logic needs a corresponding test in the same diff): `tests/test_charge.py` only exercises `ChargeAccount` through fakes; `ChargeRepository` (lines 12-33) is not exercised by any test in this diff, including `save`'s row construction and flush, and `get_latest`'s query and empty-result path. If `save` mis-maps a field, or `get_latest`'s filter is wrong, nothing here would catch it. Add tests for `ChargeRepository`, covering `save` and both the found and empty-result paths of `get_latest`.

findings.title: ChargeRequest amount and currency accepted without validation
findings.body: `ChargeRequest` (lines 12-14) accepts `amount: Decimal` and `currency: str` with no validation, and `execute` passes them straight to `self._gateway.charge` unchecked. A zero or negative `amount`, or an empty or malformed `currency`, reaches the payment gateway; depending on its behavior this can charge the wrong amount or raise an error that the `except Exception:` two lines later swallows into a silent `None`. Validate `amount > 0` and the `currency` format before calling the gateway, for example in `ChargeRequest.__post_init__` or at the start of `execute`.

findings.title: Charge transaction commit is not visible in execute
findings.body: According to custom instructions in 'Clean Architecture Boundaries' (inside a UnitOfWork a repository flushes, the use case commits): `execute` calls `self._repository.save(...)` (line 34) and returns; nothing in this file commits the transaction. `ChargeRepository.save` only calls `await self._session.flush()`, consistent with the flush-only convention, so the row stays uncommitted unless something outside this diff commits it. Not visible in the provided context whether a surrounding session or UnitOfWork commits; if not, the returned `charge_id` points to data that is rolled back at the end of the request. Confirm the commit happens, or add it to `execute`.

summary.problem: The `except Exception:` in `ChargeAccount.execute` swallows every gateway failure into a silent `None`, with no logging and no test or comment covering why.
summary.done_well: The use case, repository and test double follow the constructor-injection and flush-not-commit shape of the module, and both the happy and gateway-failure paths of `ChargeAccount.execute` are tested.
